unexplainedPanic.text: This panic stops the process and says nothing about why it can never happen. If the case can happen, return an error so a caller can handle it. If it truly cannot, say what holds in a `// Invariant: <reason>` comment directly above it or at the end of its line, so the next reader knows what they would break before changing the code around it.

invariantWithoutReason.text: This panic is marked as an invariant and gives no reason. Say what holds after `Invariant:`, such as the table built from constants or the caller that already checked, because a marker with nothing after it tells the next reader nothing and excuses nothing.

mustOutsideInitialization.text: `{{name}}` panics on a bad input, and here it runs inside a function that may be called long after the program starts, so a bad input stops the process in the middle of its work. Call it only while the package initializes, in a package-level `var` initializer or `func init()`, where a bad constant stops the program the moment it starts, or call the form that returns an error and handle it.
